expSub: Research, a startup, and production work.

bullets: Ran nearly 600,000 simulations of a widely used robot path-finding method (goal-biased RRT) in maze environments, varying one factor at a time (step size, goal bias, goal tolerance, sampling method) to isolate what drives success.

Discovered that an apparent “best” step size was a hidden artifact of sampling only whole-number coordinates: it passed 5 standard robustness checks (iteration budget, tolerance decoupling, 1,000-run replication, control maze, significance tests across 10 settings), yet vanished when the sampler was changed, with no other code change.

Showed with a wide step-size sweep (0.2–2.0) and an analysis of the planner’s design that no such optimum exists for this class of planner; ran a targeted experiment to identify the mechanism behind the artifact. Paper in preparation.
Cut assistant response time 58% (60s → 25s) by splitting each query across a multi-agent pipeline (Pydantic AI) that routes every subtask to a specialized agent.

Architected the company's MCP (Model Context Protocol) server so AI features request structured context from internal tools and data stores, with role-based access control and explicit handling when retrieval returns nothing.
Provisioned GCP infrastructure—Compute Engine for workloads that need persistent VMs, Cloud Run for HTTP services, Cloud SQL for relational state—tuning hosting cost and cold-start latency.
Delivered Tier-1 diagnostic support for desktops, laptops, classroom AV, printers, Wi-Fi, and software accounts—logging tickets, reproducing issues, and resolving or escalating with clear notes.
Maintained a digital inventory of IT assets—serial numbers, deployment locations, warranty status—so refreshes, audits, and maintenance cycles stay accountable.
Built a LangChain + FAISS RAG pipeline that answers staff questions over internal documents with citations, cutting repeat questions between coworkers by 20%.

Benchmarked 5 open-source LLMs (Llama 3, Mistral, Gemma, Qwen, Deepseek) against proprietary APIs on latency, token cost, and answer quality, using the same automated evaluation for each before recommending one for deployment.
Refined prompt templates and retrieval settings (top-k, filters, stop sequences) to reduce hallucinations, checking every change against a fixed regression set.

now.text: Competed at the 2026 ICPC North America Pacific Northwest Regional with SFBU’s Team 404NotFound: 6 problems solved, 4th place at the California site and 15th overall in Division 2.

Won 3rd place at the SFBU NVIDIA Spark Hackathon with BARRY: drive and inspect with a DOGZILLA robot dog from a Meta Quest 3S, using controllers, voice or Claude-planned goals, with live YOLO detections and a Flipper Zero badge to start missions.

Won 3rd place for Best Use of Convex at Cal Hacks 13.0 with Lobe: a shared 3D workspace where a study group explores brain MRI scans together, with live pointers, voice, a Claude assistant and quiz games on the same scans.

Released Tomville 0.2.x on PyPI: a retro terminal office where my AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) walk around as pixel pets, with a GitHub Issues task board and a Telegram bot to run the team from my phone.

Started research on robot motion planning with Dr. Satarupa Mukherjee (SFBU School of Engineering): nearly 600,000 simulations of goal-biased RRT in mazes; first-author paper in preparation. Wrapped up my founding-member role at Quiche.

Drafting two papers: AI restoration of war photographs (ethics + vignette study) and RRT with a vector maze formulation. Public repos in motion: TTorch (C++/Python autograd), Desir (agentic assistant), a real-time emotion CV stack, and a maze-solving visualizer. Tightening this minimal site to match reality.

Third place at Innovate Bay (BayHawk 2.0) for a wildfire stack: YOLOv8 + NASA FIRMS + weather context, fused with a multi-agent LLM pipeline (PydanticAI, GPT-4o, FastAPI) for severity and response planning.
HackHayward weekend: shipped KryptosProof — multi-agent, tool-using red team (sqlmap / Nuclei / FFUF), Docker sandbox, live dashboard, and signed reports for the vibe-coding security angle.

Won ThinkNext 2026 with Uniflow — a PydanticAI-orchestrated career copilot for SFBU: goal + résumé agents, RAG over courses/events, and a voice/text mock interview path with STAR-style feedback (Streamlit demo).

Joined Quiche (ADU marketplace) as a founding member — AI / DevOps focus: MCP server for contextual retrieval, multi-agent assistant design, and GCP (Compute Engine, Cloud Run, Cloud SQL) for production-shaped deploys.
Competed at ICPC Pacific Northwest Regional 2025 (Division 2). Serving as Robotics Club president this year while keeping coursework and build projects moving.
Second place at BayHack / Innovate Bay (BayHawk 1.0) with Bit for Bit: phone receipt capture → structured MongoDB + assistant layer for small-team inventory (OpenAI API, FastAPI, Node, Python).
Started as a student assistant in the SFBU IT department — Tier-1 triage for hardware/software/network tickets plus asset tracking across campus.
Finished the Sofeast LLM internship (May–Aug 2025): internal RAG/LLM systems, evaluation and deployment tooling, and shipping models into real business workflows.
Top 3 at SFBU IEEE Mind Sparks with BleuLaMuse — GPT + FAISS + Streamlit career chatbot with modular backend for later cloud expansion.
